name: Binance BTC/USDT observable level-two liquidity shock
description: Compares the current Binance observable five-basis-point base depth and spread in basis points with the arithmetic mean of the prior 60 valid one-second Binance book observations. The Binance input is the full displayed level-two book this repository reconstructs locally. depth_ratio_60s and spread_ratio_60s expose the continuous change. State is shock when depth is at or below 0.50 of baseline or spread is at or above 2.0 times baseline; thinning below 0.75 depth or above 1.5 spread; recovering when the immediately prior state was shock and the current observation has left shock but remains thinning; otherwise normal. The 0.50, 0.75, 1.5, and 2.0 classification boundaries are initial research thresholds that require empirical calibration. Missing, non-ready, or non-contiguous one-second Binance book observations break continuity and restart warm-up. This level-two signal measures observable thinning and widening; it does not attribute a change to cancellation or execution. This identity is single-venue: it reads only Binance inputs and is ready whenever the Binance book has 60 contiguous one-second observations and is inside the staleness bound, independently of the other adopted spot venue. The blended `btc.external.*` reading of the same measurement stays the reference layer and continues to require every adopted venue (ADR 0024). Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even. Venue port (B1): this identity is the Binance sibling of `btc.coinbase.liquidity_shock@1.0.0` and reuses that definition's formulas, windows, thresholds, warm-up, staleness bound, field set, field types and eight-place round-half-to-even rounding verbatim; only the source ids differ (`crates/btc-signals/src/spot_signals.rs`, `crates/btc-signals/src/candidate_spot_signals.rs`). The instrument is Binance spot BTCUSDT; this identity publishes no price-level field, so its outputs (base sizes, basis points, imbalances, ratios, counts) are quote-currency neutral and nothing is converted. Binance inputs are rights-gated (`signals/knowledge/RIGHTS-LEDGER.md`): the lane is built and tested to the adopted standard, and its runtime refuses to start unless the environment allow-list `SIGNALS_ENABLED_VENUES` names `binance`, which the deployment sets only after that row clears. The Binance book input is the `btcusdt@depth20@100ms` partial-depth stream: every message is a complete top-20-per-side image at a 100 ms cadence, not a diff, and it carries no venue clock, so `event_time_basis` is `receipt` and `event_time` is the local receipt time. Ordering is the strictly increasing `last_update_id`; a duplicate or lower id is dropped and never applied. The captured window is 20 levels per side. An observation whose five-basis-point band reaches the outermost captured level on either side is not fully observed: it is not ready and publishes the instance-state reason `binance_band_exceeds_captured_depth` rather than a lower-bound depth. quote_currency is emitted on every decision and is the constant "usd" for this venue: this identity publishes no price-denominated field — its outputs are base sizes, ratios, basis-point and count fields, all quote-currency neutral — so nothing is converted. E47 (USD quoting): this identity quotes in USD and publishes no price, notional or quote-denominated cost field — its outputs are base sizes, counts, basis-point ratios and durations, which are quote-currency neutral — so nothing is converted and no usdt_usd_rate is published. quote_currency is the constant "usd".
